findings.title: scripts/effect-budget.json still budgets effects this PR removed or justified
findings.body: The `react-effect-budget` rule only fails when a file's unjustified effect count exceeds its budget (`oxlint-plugin-t3code/rules/react-effect-budget.ts:61`). Justified effects, like the two annotated here, are not counted. The budget file is not touched, so it still allows 2 for `panelAnimations.ts` (line 426), 3 for `SshPasswordPromptDialog.tsx` (301), 1 each for `BackgroundThreadAnnouncer.tsx`, `ConfirmDialogHost.tsx`, `QuitHoldOverlay.tsx`, `mainAppLocation.ts`, `useDesktopLocalBootstraps.ts`, `useLiveRegion.ts`, `useThreadVisitedMigration.ts` and `remoteOpen.ts`, and an entry for the deleted `hooks/useNavigateBack.ts` (416). Each of those files now has 0 unjustified effects, so each has headroom for a new unreviewed effect. That defeats the budget. Lower these entries to the real counts and drop the deleted file's entry. `AppSidebarLayout.tsx` and `PullRequestsPage.tsx` need the same check.

findings.title: Do the app-lifetime shell subscriptions change behavior before authentication?
findings.body: `startBackgroundThreadAnnouncements` and `startThreadVisitedMigration` used to run only inside `AppSidebarLayout`, which `__root.tsx` renders after the auth gate. They now subscribe to `quietThreadShellsAtom`, `threadShellsAtom` and `liveShellEnvironmentIdsAtom` on `appAtomRegistry` at page start, including on `/pair`, `/connect`, the guest page and unauthenticated routes. Mounting these atoms evaluates `environmentThreadsAtom(environmentId)` for every enabled catalog environment (`packages/client-runtime/src/state/threadShell.ts:376-383`). Does that start shell or connection subscriptions earlier than before, for example against an environment that has not authenticated yet? If it does, the visit migration could also fire `threadEnvironment.visit` commands from a page that previously never ran it. If these atoms only read already-connected state, ignore this.

findings.title: Escape-to-leave on pull requests moved to a new dispatcher scope with no test
findings.body: `useEscapeToGoBack` is replaced by `registerPullRequestsEscapeCommand`. The branch between `history.back()` and `navigate('/')` on `__TSR_index`, the pathname gate, and the `consumed` check are all new logic, and none has a test. The dispatcher's observer ordering is covered in `shortcuts/dispatcher.browser.test.ts`, but nothing covers this command. The old hook had no test either, so this is a gap, not a regression. A small browser test that Escape on `/pull-requests` goes back or navigates home, and does nothing when a dialog consumed the key, would pin the moved behavior.

contracts.action: Queue SSH password prompts at app start so a prompt that arrives before the dialog mounts is kept
contracts.equivalent_path: The old component subscribed to `window.desktopBridge.onSshPasswordPrompt` in its own mount effect and held the queue in React state.
contracts.before_after: Before, a prompt delivered while the dialog was unmounted (pairing or sign-in pages) was dropped. Now `startSshPasswordPromptQueue` in `appInit.tsx:136` subscribes once and appends to a module-level queue. The dialog reads it with `useSyncExternalStore` and mounts only the head request. `removeSshPasswordPrompt` still removes only the head request, as before.
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog shows the queued prompt once `SshPasswordPromptDialog` mounts in `__root.tsx:239`. If the prompt expired meanwhile, `useDeadlinePassed` shows 'Expired' with a Dismiss button.
contracts.failure_mode: If the dialog never mounts, the queue is not bounded and an expired prompt stays until dismissed. A missing `onSshPasswordPrompt` falls back to a no-op unsubscribe. Responding failures show an error in the dialog and the prompt stays.

contracts.action: Pull requests Escape-to-go-back becomes a post-dispatch observer scope in the app shell
contracts.equivalent_path: The old `useEscapeToGoBack` in `PullRequestsPage` was a window keydown listener that skipped `event.defaultPrevented`, blurred the active element, then went back or navigated to `/`.
contracts.before_after: The new observer in `dispatcher.ts:84` runs after the scopes. Its `consumed` flag includes `defaultPrevented`, so the skip is equivalent. It gates on pathname `/pull-requests` instead of the page being mounted. `__TSR_index !== 0` matches what `useCanGoBack` checked.
contracts.visible_effect: Escape on the pull requests page behaves as before.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. Observers never consume the key, but this one calls `preventDefault` itself.

contracts.action: Probe remote-capable editors once per page via a keepAlive atom
contracts.equivalent_path: The old `useRemoteCapableEditors` cached a module variable and probed in an effect; the failure path fell back to `vscode`.
contracts.before_after: The old code cached the fallback when the probe was undefined, rejected or empty. The new code starts the probe on first atom read and replaces the fallback only for a non-empty remote-capable result. A rejection is swallowed and the fallback stays, so the visible result is the same.
contracts.visible_effect: The editor picker shows `vscode` until the probe resolves, then the probed list.
contracts.failure_mode: The probe has no timeout, so a never-resolving bridge call leaves the fallback list for the page's life. This matches the old behavior.

contracts.action: Background thread announcements and the visited migration run from app start, outside React
contracts.equivalent_path: The old announcer was a component using `useQuietThreadShells`, `useThreadRouteTarget` and a composer-draft selector, mounted inside `AppSidebarLayout`.
contracts.before_after: The open-thread key is now read from `router.state.matches.at(-1)?.params`, which matches the old hook's params (environmentId, threadId, draftId). The draft store subscription is short-circuited unless the open thread changes. Announcements are dropped while no region element is attached, but `memory` still advances.
contracts.visible_effect: Screen-reader announcements for background threads work as before inside the shell.
contracts.failure_mode: Status changes that happen while the shell is not mounted are recorded in memory and never spoken. Whether early atom mounting has side effects before auth is unconfirmed (see finding).
contracts.open_question: Does mounting `quietThreadShellsAtom` and `threadShellsAtom` before the auth gate start environment subscriptions that previously began only after authentication?

summary: The refactor moves several app-shell effects into app-lifetime services and external stores, and I found no functional defect in it. The SSH prompt fix works as intended: the queue starts at app init and the dialog reads it with `useSyncExternalStore`. The Escape handler matches the old `consumed`, `defaultPrevented` and `canGoBack` semantics. The confirm-dialog host count, the live region and the quit-hint store are equivalent to their old versions. I raised three non-blocking points: `scripts/effect-budget.json` was not updated and now leaves headroom for unreviewed effects in about ten files, a low-confidence question about whether subscribing to thread-shell atoms at app start changes pre-auth behavior, and no test for the moved Escape command.
